note: The livecheck table (python -m wtdd.livecheck --list). One entry per hardware step. Keys: item (the roadmap item), step (<item>.<k>, k = the number or letter of the line under **Needs the dog** in that item's PR, the k of the evening's `live <item> <k>`), pr (the PR number the title is read from; null for a night-2 goal section), title (that Needs-the-dog line, verbatim), do (the physical action in one line, with what the eyes must confirm that no row can), rows (the ledger rows that must land, in order: {tool, agent?, ok, where: {dotted.path: value | {gte, lte, in, re}}}; empty = unchecked, cannot PASS), fatal_warns (regexes over the API log; a match is FAIL with the line), unsafe (only rows landing after the check starts count; {tool: T, before: U}: the order T then U is forbidden, the U row that completes it decides and is printed `U after T`; {tool: T, between: [A, B]}: a T row after an A row and before any B row is UNSAFE, the T row decides), timeout_s (FAIL when this many seconds have passed since the check started and a row is still missing; --timeout overrides it), settle_s (after the last row matched, keep watching the log and the unsafe patterns this long before PASS; 0 = PASS at once), note (what is a guess until the first live run). Thresholds marked UNVERIFIED were never read from a dog.

steps.title: `frame_id` must be `odom`. The grid refuses any later frame whose `frame_id` differs, so a mismatch shows as a rising `cb_errors` on `GET /dog/lidar` and `GET /dog/grid`, paired with `WARN lidar frame callback failed err=ValueError: frame_id ...` on stderr.
steps.do: API up from the repo checkout; connect from the page; POST /dog/lidar {on: true}; eyes: the `[wtdd:dog] first lidar frame frame_id=odom` line in the API terminal, center_vs_odom_m under 1 m.
fatal_warns: WARN lidar window center is far from
steps.note: settle_s 20: the frames arrive after the connect row, so the frame_id refusal (a WARN, no row) can only be seen by waiting. UNVERIFIED: the first live frame.

steps.title: Read `z_layers` on the same first-frame line to find where the floor sits. If the floor falls inside the band, tune `lidar.Z_MIN` / `Z_MAX` (0.10..1.00 today, a guess).
steps.do: Eyes only: read z_layers on the first-frame line; the floor below 0.10 m, the walls inside 0.10..1.00; else set Z_MIN/Z_MAX once and commit before filming. No row is written.
steps.note: unchecked: a number a person reads, no device row.

steps.title: Walk about 3 m and watch `GET /dog/grid`. If `extent_m` grows while a wall's cells stay put, the window `origin` moves with the dog as the fixture assumes. If the grid smears into a streak, the points are body-relative and this item's frame assumption is wrong: STOP, do not tune; the fix is a different transform, not a threshold.
steps.do: Drag the dog to where it stands (the tie); POST /dog/grid {save: true} once, standing still; hand-drive 3 m along one wall; POST /dog/grid {save: true} again. Eyes: the wall's cells stay put on the page while the extent grows (a streak = STOP).
fatal_warns: WARN lidar window center is far from
steps.note: UNVERIFIED guesses: frames gte 30 (5-10 Hz over a 10 s drive), cells gte 100, extent_m gte 3. The two saves put the growth in two rows a person reads side by side; the cells staying put is the eye's.

steps.title: `GET /dog/lidar`: `grid_frames` should track `n`, and `cb_errors` should stay 0. A non-zero `cb_errors` names its refusal (frame_id, resolution or `MAX_SIDE`) in the WARN line.
steps.do: Eyes only: curl GET /dog/lidar twice a few seconds apart; grid_frames tracks n, cb_errors 0. A GET writes no row.
steps.note: unchecked: a read, no device row.

steps.title: The per-frame accumulate cost on the driver's dispatcher is the `ms=` on the `[wtdd:dog] grid frames=... ms=...` line, logged every 100th frame. It must stay well under the frame period (5-10 Hz); on the 3-4k-voxel fixture it is 1-5 ms and a real frame may hold ten times the voxels.
steps.do: Eyes only: read ms= on the `grid frames=` lines in the API terminal; well under 100 ms.
steps.note: unchecked: a number a person reads off the log, no device row.

steps.title: `POST /dog/grid {save: true}` must write one `dog.grid_save` row with `cal_at` set. Restart the API: the page should draw the saved grid with `source` `ui/grid.json`, through the calibration saved with it.
steps.do: POST /dog/grid {save: true}; then restart the API and reload the page. Eyes: the grid label reads `ui/grid.json` and the walls sit where they sat.
steps.note: The restart and the redraw are the eye's; the row with cal_at is the device's.

steps.title: After a power cycle the `[wtdd:dog] WARN grid kept across the reconnect` line must appear. Then `POST /dog/grid {clear: true, why: "power cycle"}` (one `dog.grid_clear` row), and a fresh grid should start on the next frame (`[wtdd:dog] grid started`).
steps.do: Power-cycle the dog; reconnect from the page; POST /dog/grid {clear: true, why: "power cycle"}. Eyes: `WARN grid kept across the reconnect` (expected here, not fatal) then `grid started` in the API terminal.
steps.note: args.why is the string posted (feat/01-occupancy session.grid_clear: args {why, frames_before, cells_before}).
